key_insight: Physical noise structure creates approximate Pauli-fidelity symmetries under gate conjugation, allowing gauge fixing without knowing error magnitudes.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical way to separate SPAM errors from gate noise and improve error characterization in quantum hardware calibration.
method: Apply Lindbladian perturbation theory to realistic Clifford gates.
Derive symmetry relations between Pauli fidelities and their gate-conjugates.
Use selection rules to identify which dissipative errors can break symmetry at first order.
evidence_signal: The paper reports analytic results plus numerical and experimental validation on IBM Kingston, showing coherent errors are first-order symmetric while common T1 and T2φ noise only create asymmetry at second order.
watch_item: The symmetry-based gauge fixing is approximate and depends on correctly identifying the dominant error type; strong nonideal or higher-order noise may weaken the assumptions.
paper_title: Symmetries of Pauli Noise from Lindbladian Dynamics
